title.narrative: Provision of life-saving WASH assistance to the most vulnerable communities in underserved and hard-to-reach areas to address the impact of dry conditions and mitigate displacements in Bu'ale District

description.narrative: ltpgtRDSA will target a population of 15,804 individuals (5,294 women, 4,290 girls, 3,270 men, and 2,950 boys) in Buale district. The target populations of this project are both displaced and vulnerable host communities in Buale District struggling with harsh climatic conditions. The population comprises 6,322 IDP individuals and 9,482 vulnerable host community individuals who will benefit from this project.ltbrgtThe project will focus on underserved displacement sites and vulnerable host community settlements, improving access to WASH services by implementing context-relevant and needs-driven WASH activities. In this project, RDSA aims to reduce the distance and waiting time for WASH services at the community level by investing in the installation of water systems within IDP sites. As part of RDSA’s strategy and that of the allocation community, ownership and sustainability will be enhanced through community participation and capacity building therefore, in the project sites, RDSA will rehabilitate 1 strategic drought-proof borehole equipped with a generator, solar panel, and pump and spare part tools to replace the old pipes in Bulagaduud village of Buale District. Additionally, RDSA will provide emergency water provision to 1,000 HHs displaced from the Buale District. This will be served through the construction of two water kiosks with pipeline extensions. RDSA will also train 5 community members (OM), inclusive of all genders and disability and diversity (2 women 3 men), as water source management committees in basic operation, maintenance, and conflict resolution modules. RDSA will undertake regular water treatments at the source (well chlorination). RDSA will distribute 2,134 hygiene kits to families assessed as most in need and susceptible to AWD/cholera outbreaks and prioritize Households with a history of WASH-scarce-related diseases to access adequate water for their domestic use. Sanitation facilities will be improved through the construction of 63 gender-segregated floodproof emergency latrines with handwashing stations, targeting at least 2500 individuals 15% (9) of the latrines will be disability-friendly. ltbrgtSolar lights will be installed in the latrines to provide a safe environment for nighttime usage and mitigate the risk of GBV and other safety- and security-related fears. In this project, RDSA will mobilize community members to informally take control of latrine management as a way to enhance cleaning, rehabilitation, and equitable access to the latrines. (8) Sets of sanitation tool kits will be distributed to IDP sites and host community villages to enable them to clean up latrines and social sites and allow them to divert floodwaters from their residential sites and homes. RDSA will carry out a KAP survey at the start of the project to help the RDSA WASH team design context- and culturally appropriate content and approaches for hygiene education awareness sessions and the composition of emergency hygiene kits an end-line KAP survey will also be conducted to measure the change in knowledge, attitude, and practice during the project period. A refresher training of 10 community-level hygiene promotion volunteers (6 women, 4 men) will be done to enhance their capacity to lead hygiene promotion. Priority will be given to disabled, women- and child-headed households, minorities, and marginalized families.ltbrgtlt/pgt
